intro: Field Trip Health Thunder Bay runs ketamine-assisted psychotherapy out of a small clinic at the back of 153 Algoma Street South, in the downtown Port Arthur part of the city. It sees adults with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain and substance use problems, and it is the only Field Trip clinic in Northwestern Ontario.

This is outpatient care. You come in on a weekday, stay a couple of hours and leave with a driver. The local team includes registered nurses who are also psychotherapists, and the clinic says it serves veterans, first responders, healthcare workers and Indigenous communities from across the region, as far as Dryden, Fort Frances and Sioux Lookout.

pillars.title: About two hours with a therapist beside you
pillars.body: A Thunder Bay dosing session takes about 2 hours and 15 minutes. You recline in a zero-gravity chair under a weighted blanket, with noise-cancelling headphones and music, after a nurse gives a low dose of ketamine. Your therapist stays for the whole session and talks it through with you at the end. Because you may be drowsy, you cannot drive home that day.

pillars.title: A side door in Port Arthur
pillars.body: Don't go in the front. The front of 153 Algoma Street South is an unrelated walk-in clinic, and Field Trip's entrance is at the back of the building. That door is usually locked, so knock and someone will let you in. Inside, there are five steps up at the entrance, which means the clinic is not wheelchair accessible right now. Parking is free in the lot beside it, and service animals are welcome.

pillars.title: Nurses who are also therapists
pillars.body: Erin Pomanti is a registered nurse and psychotherapist who has worked in mental health since 2015, starting at Lakehead Psychiatric Hospital. Chad Beaver and Michelle Gamble are registered psychotherapists with over 22 years of clinical work each, much of it with trauma, anxiety and depression. Registered nurse Kathleen Crnkovic and a group of nurse practitioners handle the medical side.

overviewH2: How treatment is set up in Thunder Bay
overview: Everyone starts with a free 15-minute discovery call, followed by a questionnaire and a 50-minute medical consultation with a nurse practitioner. OHIP does not cover that consultation. The nurse practitioner checks for things that make the treatment unsafe, such as pregnancy, a history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled high blood pressure or a recent severe head injury, and reviews your medications.

If you go ahead, the usual plan is 6 or 9 dosing sessions. In Thunder Bay a session lasts about 2 hours and 15 minutes, a little shorter than at some other Field Trip clinics, and the medicine is mostly given by intramuscular injection. A therapist sits with you throughout, then helps you make sense of the experience in integration sessions.

location.heading: Field Trip Health Thunder Bay in Thunder Bay, Ontario
location.intro: The clinic is on Algoma Street South in downtown Port Arthur, the north end of Thunder Bay, close to the waterfront. Shuniah and Kakabeka Falls are about 20 to 30 minutes away by car, Nipigon around an hour and a quarter, and Dryden or Fort Frances about three and a half to four hours, while Toronto is a 2-hour flight or a very long drive.

faqIntro: Answers are based on the Thunder Bay clinic's page on fieldtriphealth.ca. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Field Trip Health Thunder Bay a live-in rehab?
faqs.a: No. It is an outpatient clinic open on weekdays, and you go home after every appointment. It has no beds and offers no detox. For residential addiction treatment or medically supervised withdrawal, ask the care team about options or look at residential centres in Northwestern Ontario and beyond.

faqs.q: What does the Thunder Bay clinic treat?
faqs.a: Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy here is used mainly for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction and chronic pain, usually after standard treatments have not given enough relief. The therapists also support people with grief, ADHD, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, complex PTSD, Indigenous trauma and relationship issues. Results are different for everyone.

faqs.q: How long is a session in Thunder Bay?
faqs.a: About 2 hours and 15 minutes, including preparation, the medicine and integration support. Standard plans include 6 or 9 dosing sessions, and the team meets with you at the end to plan any ongoing care.

faqs.q: What does it cost, and will insurance pay?
faqs.a: Field Trip Health does not publish its prices; they depend on the number of sessions and how the medicine is given, and the team explains them on a free discovery call. The nurse practitioner consultation has a fee, since OHIP does not cover it. Public plans do not pay for the medical part, but psychotherapy or nursing benefits from an extended health plan often cover some of it, and outside financing is available.

faqs.q: How do I find the clinic entrance?
faqs.a: Use the back entrance of 153 Algoma Street South. The front of the building is a separate walk-in clinic, and the Field Trip door at the rear is usually locked, so knock to be let in. Free parking is in the lot beside the clinic.

faqs.q: Is the Thunder Bay clinic wheelchair accessible?
faqs.a: No, not at the moment. There are five steps at the entrance, so the clinic is not currently wheelchair accessible. Service animals are welcome. If stairs are a problem, mention it on your discovery call.

faqs.q: Who is on the care team?
faqs.a: The Thunder Bay team includes registered nurse psychotherapists, registered social workers and registered psychotherapists trained in trauma-informed psychedelic-assisted therapy. Named staff include Erin Pomanti, RN and psychotherapist, and psychotherapists Chad Beaver and Michelle Gamble. Nurse practitioners do the medical screening.

faqs.q: Who is eligible, and do I need a referral?
faqs.a: You can contact the clinic yourself; a referral is not required, though doctors can refer through Field Trip's form or Ocean eReferral. A nurse practitioner decides eligibility. The treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, allergic to the medicine, have had schizophrenia or psychosis, or have uncontrolled hypertension or a recent severe head injury.

faqs.q: How should I prepare for a dosing session?
faqs.a: Avoid alcohol and recreational substances beforehand, and eat something light rather than a heavy meal. You will not be able to drive afterwards, so line up a ride home before the day.

faqs.q: Is Field Trip Health Thunder Bay still open?
faqs.a: Yes. In October 2026 the clinic's page on fieldtriphealth.ca listed its address, weekday hours and staff, and bookings go through the Field Trip Health Canada site. The Canadian clinics have been run separately from the US business since a 2023 restructuring, when the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing took them over.
